Earnings growth is 51% over five years and 71% over three, and at a P/E of 24.5 that's a PEG of 0.48, well inside my buy zone. Growth that fast makes me nervous about how long it lasts, and I can't see earnings consistency, free cash flow, margins, insider buying or institutional ownership in this snapshot. I'm not making up an intrinsic value either, so I've set it equal to the price, which is a placeholder rather than an estimate. I keep the shares, let the winner run as I'd never cut the flowers to water the weeds, and add only once the missing checks come back clean.

exit_trigger: Sell at a cyclical peak: earnings at multi-year highs, P/E compressing toward normal, euphoric sentiment; Sell if earnings keep declining for 3 or more consecutive quarters with no sign of a trough; Sell if debt-to-equity rises meaningfully above 0.6 without a plan to delever; Sell if inventory growth outpaces sales growth; Sell if the dividend is cut or multiple executives sell shares in the same 90 days; Sell if PEG expands above 2.0
rationale: I own this one, and I call it a cyclical, not the stalwart the screen suggests, because homebuilders live and die by the housing cycle. The numbers look cheap on the surface: P/E of 10.4, PEG of 0.65, PEGY of 0.56 and debt-to-equity of just 0.27. But 5-year growth of 16.2% against a 3-year figure of -4.6% tells me earnings have rolled over, and with a cyclical a low P/E can be a warning sign, not a bargain. This filing does not report capacity utilization, inventory versus sales, insider buying or ownership, or free cash flow and margin trends, so I could not check those criteria and my confidence stays low. I'm holding my small position, down 4.8% so far, and not adding until I can see whether earnings are bottoming or still falling. I'm also not selling into weakness while the balance sheet is this sound and the thesis isn't broken. I'd have no problem sitting through this in my stomach, and I'd be ready to sell if the balance sheet slips.

exit_trigger: Earnings growth decelerates below 15% AND PEG rises above 1.5; PEG expands above 2.0; Story changes materially: orders or earnings turn down for 3 consecutive quarters; Balance sheet deteriorates: debt-to-equity rises above 0.5; Evidence emerges of serial acquisitions or heavy insider selling by multiple executives
rationale: I own POWL, and the shares are down 21.4% from my $194.11 entry after 109 days. I'm not selling on price alone, because the business numbers haven't broken. Five-year growth is 27.3% and three-year growth is 51.4%, and a P/E of 25.25 gives a PEG of 0.93, which is Fast Grower buy territory. Debt-to-equity is reported at 0.0. By my own rule, a fairly priced stock has a P/E equal to its growth rate, and that puts fair value around $165, so the margin of safety is thin at about 7%. I keep the position and don't add. Insider activity, institutional ownership, free cash flow and margin trends are not reported in this snapshot, so my conviction is moderate. I would rather hold what I can see than water the weeds, and I would sell only if the growth story breaks.
